links.scope: Injection pass ordering, off-lock collection, refusal before storage, authority and mutation recipients, next-turn history, plus specialized cancellation, late-failure and Python model-transport evidence.
links.review: Read the exact assertions against §9.4 and their Python reference tests. Event aliases in mutation injections are resolved before return, so a missing target cannot masquerade as an authorization refusal. The forced Python _name_held failure after a blocked decision has no fallible counterpart in Rust: delivery_keys::Named::decided returns immediately for result.blocked; driver::inbound::Record::decide then records the decision without a user callback. Existing failed-lock-release scenarios are not asserted to exercise that private fault point. Re-read after making the two interleaving fixtures' lock manager explicit: the same steps and assertions establish separate locked passes with a controlled FIFO queue; the backing store remains the runner's store.
